tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the man say he did before buying the blender?

options.A: Read numerous comments users put online.
options.B: Blended all his food without using a machine.
options.C: Searched for the state-of-the-art models of blenders.
options.D: Did thorough research on the price of kitchen appliances.

questions.cn: 男士说他买搅拌机之前做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 读了用户在网上发表的大量评论。
optionsCn.B: 不用机器就把所有食物都搅碎。
optionsCn.C: 搜寻最新型号的搅拌机。
optionsCn.D: 对厨房小家电的价格做了充分研究。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she has never thought of doing?

options.A: Eating any blended food.
options.B: Buying a blender herself.
options.C: Using machines to do her cooking.
options.D: Making soups and juices for herself.

questions.cn: 女士说她从来没想过做什么？

optionsCn.A: 吃任何搅碎的食物。
optionsCn.B: 自己买一台搅拌机。
optionsCn.C: 用机器做饭。
optionsCn.D: 给自己做汤和果汁。

questions.stem: What does the man say is a really healthy habit?

options.A: Cooking every meal creatively in the kitchen.
options.B: Paying due attention to his personal hygiene.
options.C: Eating breakfast punctually every morning.
options.D: Making his own fresh fruit juice regularly.

questions.cn: 男士说什么是一个真正健康的习惯？

optionsCn.A: 每顿饭都在厨房里创意地烹饪。
optionsCn.B: 适当注意个人卫生。
optionsCn.C: 每天准时吃早餐。
optionsCn.D: 定期自己做鲜榨果汁。

questions.stem: What do we learn about store-bought juice from the conversation?

options.A: One-tenth of it is sugar.
options.B: It looks healthy and attractive.
options.C: One’s fancy may be tickled by it.
options.D: It contains an assortment of nutrients.

questions.cn: 从对话中我们了解到店里买的果汁什么情况？

optionsCn.A: 它有十分之一是糖。
optionsCn.B: 它看起来健康诱人。
optionsCn.C: 它可能勾起人的兴趣。
optionsCn.D: 它含有各种养分。

lines.t: I’ve just bought a new blender.
lines.cn: 我刚买了一个新的搅拌机。

lines.t: What’s that?
lines.cn: 那是什么？

lines.t: A blender, you know, a machine that blends food.
lines.cn: 搅拌机，就是那种把食物打碎的机器。

lines.t: Uh, yes, of course, the electric kitchen appliance.
lines.cn: 呃，是的，当然，厨房电动小家电。

lines.t: Exactly, this one is state-of-the-art.
lines.cn: 没错，这台是最新款的。

lines.t: I’ve been meaning to buy one for a while, and I did thorough research on which specific model to get.
lines.cn: 我想买一台有一阵子了，还认真研究过该买哪个具体型号。

lines.t: I read through maybe hundreds of online user reviews.
lines.cn: 我大概读了几百条线上用户评论。

lines.t: Anyway, it’s amazing.
lines.cn: 总之，它棒极了。

lines.t: Really?
lines.cn: 真的吗？

lines.t: What could be so special about it?
lines.cn: 它能有什么特别的？

lines.t: I mean it’s just a blender.
lines.cn: 我是说，它不就是台搅拌机吗。

lines.t: Well, basically, it’s just a very good one.
lines.cn: 嗯，基本上，它就是一台非常好的搅拌机。

lines.t: It feels heavy and sturdy and well made.
lines.cn: 手感厚重、结实，做工很好。

lines.t: It also has lots of power and can easily cut and crush practically anything.
lines.cn: 而且功率很大，几乎什么都能轻松切碎、打烂。

lines.t: This way, the soups and juices I make come out really fine and smooth, with no lumpy bits.
lines.cn: 这样，我做的汤和果汁就特别细腻顺滑，没有结块。

lines.t: Um, I see.
lines.cn: 呃，我明白了。

lines.t: I’ve never thought of getting one myself.
lines.cn: 我自己从没想过要买一台。

lines.t: It sounds like the kind of thing that, for me personally, I would rarely use.
lines.cn: 听起来，对我个人来说，这类东西我很少会用上。

lines.t: I’ve never had one before, and now that I do.
lines.cn: 我以前从没有过，现在有了，

lines.t: I use it all the time.
lines.cn: 我一直在用。

lines.t: I make a fresh fruit juice in the morning.
lines.cn: 我早上会做一杯鲜榨果汁。

lines.t: maybe not every morning, but three or four times a week, and it feels fantastic.
lines.cn: 也许不是每天早上，但一周三四次，感觉特别好。

lines.t: It’s a really healthy habit.
lines.cn: 这是个非常健康的习惯。

lines.t: I can imagine that must feel quite satisfying.
lines.cn: 我可以想象那一定很有满足感。

lines.t: I can picture you getting all creative in the kitchen and trying out a multitude of different ingredients,
lines.cn: 我能想象你在厨房里创意大发，尝试各种各样的食材，

lines.t: and it’s obviously going to be healthier than buying packaged juice from a supermarket.
lines.cn: 而且它显然比从超市买包装果汁更健康。

lines.t: It’s so much healthier.
lines.cn: 健康太多了。

lines.t: It’s not even close.
lines.cn: 完全没法比。

lines.t: Did you know that store-bought juice is like 10% sugar?
lines.cn: 你知道吗，店里买的果汁差不多有 10% 是糖？

lines.t: Right, so then you bought it for the health benefits?
lines.cn: 好，那你买它就是为了健康的好处？

lines.t: Mostly yes.
lines.cn: 主要是。

lines.t: Basically, it allows me to have a more varied diet with a far wider assortment of nutrients,
lines.cn: 基本上，它让我能饮食更多样，摄入的养分种类也丰富得多，

lines.t: because it’s not only fruit in my morning juices you see.
lines.cn: 因为你看，我早上的果汁里可不只有水果。

lines.t: I can also throw in vegetables, nuts, yogurts, cereals, anything that tickles my fancy.
lines.cn: 我还能加蔬菜、坚果、酸奶、麦片，任何我感兴趣的东西。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is the question the woman asked Mr. Grimm after the introduction?

options.A: How he has made himself popular as the mayor of Berkton.
options.B: How the residents will turn Berkton into a tourist attraction.
options.C: How charming he himself considers the village of Berkton to be.
options.D: How he has led people of Berkton to change the village radically.

questions.cn: 在介绍之后，女士向格林先生提出了什么问题？

optionsCn.A: 他是如何让自己成为受欢迎的伯克顿镇长的。
optionsCn.B: 居民们将如何把伯克顿变成旅游胜地。
optionsCn.C: 他本人觉得伯克顿有多迷人。
optionsCn.D: 他是如何带领伯克顿人彻底改变村庄的。

questions.stem: What do we learn about Berkton of 10 years ago?

options.A: It was developed only to a limited extent.
options.B: It was totally isolated as a sleepy village.
options.C: It was relatively unknown to the outside.
options.D: It was endowed with rare natural resources.

questions.cn: 关于 10 年前的伯克顿，我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 它的开发程度有限。
optionsCn.B: 它作为宁静小村与世隔绝。
optionsCn.C: 外界对它相对知之甚少。
optionsCn.D: 它拥有稀有的自然资源。

questions.stem: What resulted from the passing of the legislative proposal “Motion 836”?

options.A: All the properties in Berkton were designed by the same architect.
options.B: The majority of residents lived in harmony with their neighbors.
options.C: The majority of residents enjoyed cosy housing conditions.
options.D: All the houses in Berkton looked aesthetically similar.

questions.cn: 立法提案“第 836 号动议”的通过带来了什么结果？

optionsCn.A: 伯克顿所有房产都由同一位建筑师设计。
optionsCn.B: 大多数居民与邻居和睦相处。
optionsCn.C: 大多数居民享有舒适的住房条件。
optionsCn.D: 伯克顿所有房屋外观相似。

questions.stem: Why does the man say the tourists are a blessing to Berkton?

options.A: They have helped boost the local economy.
options.B: They have made the residents unusually proud.
options.C: They have contributed considerably to its popularity.
options.D: They have brought happiness to everyone in the village.

questions.cn: 男士为什么说游客对伯克顿是种福气？

optionsCn.A: 他们帮助提振了本地经济。
optionsCn.B: 他们让居民格外自豪。
optionsCn.C: 他们大大提升了这里的知名度。
optionsCn.D: 他们给村里每个人带来了快乐。

lines.t: Today we have a very interesting guest.
lines.cn: 今天我们请到一位很有意思的嘉宾。

lines.t: Mr. Thomas Benjamin Grimm, the mayor of Berkton, is here to talk about his job and responsibilities overseeing this charming village.
lines.cn: 伯克顿镇镇长托马斯·本杰明·格林先生来到这里，谈谈他管理这座迷人村庄的工作与职责。

lines.t: Mr. Grimm, thank you for being here.
lines.cn: 格林先生，感谢您到来。

lines.t: Thank you for having me.
lines.cn: 谢谢你的邀请。

lines.t: I’d like to start by stating the obvious.
lines.cn: 我想从显而易见的事说起。

lines.t: Berkton has become one of the most popular tourist destinations in the country, and this has happened under your watch.
lines.cn: 伯克顿已成为全国最受欢迎的旅游目的地之一，而这发生在您主政期间。

lines.t: Just how did you achieve this?
lines.cn: 您究竟是怎么做到的？

lines.t: The achievement belongs to all the residents of Berkton.
lines.cn: 这一成就是所有伯克顿居民共同取得的。

lines.t: It was a shared effort where everybody pitched in for the communal good.
lines.cn: 这是一次共同的努力，每个人都为公共利益出了力。

lines.t: But how did this change happen?
lines.cn: 但这一变化是怎么发生的呢？

lines.t: In about 10 years, Berkton has gone from a relatively unheard-of sleepy village to a must-see destination.
lines.cn: 在大约 10 年里，伯克顿从一个相对默默无闻、宁静安逸的小村，变成了必看的目的地。

lines.t: Yes, the change has truly been remarkable.
lines.cn: 是的，这一变化确实非同寻常。

lines.t: Berkton was always fortunate to be endowed with such a beautiful natural allure.
lines.cn: 伯克顿一直有幸拥有如此美丽的自然魅力。

lines.t: The Ambury Hills above the village remain untouched by human development, and the Sonora Valley just below it is equally stunning.
lines.cn: 村庄上方的安伯里山丘至今未被人类开发触及，而它下方的索诺拉谷同样令人惊叹。

lines.t: The transformation commenced in a town hall meeting in spring 2008 over 10 years ago now, when an overwhelming majority of neighbors voted in favor of “Motion 836”.
lines.cn: 转变始于 2008 年春——距今十多年前——的一次镇民大会，当时绝大多数邻居投票赞成“第 836 号动议”。

lines.t: This legislative proposal essentially set out to harmonize the aesthetic appearance of all the houses in Berkton.
lines.cn: 这项立法提案的主旨是统一伯克顿所有房屋的外观美学。

lines.t: The idea was that if all the properties looked a certain way with shared design features, then a village as a whole would look more beautiful.
lines.cn: 其想法是：如果所有房产都呈现某种特定样式、具有共同的设计特征，那么整个村庄看起来就会更美。

lines.t: And it worked.
lines.cn: 而这奏效了。

lines.t: It certainly did.
lines.cn: 确实如此。

lines.t: I’m looking now at a before-and-after photo, and the change is truly remarkable.
lines.cn: 我现在正看着一张前后对比照，变化实在惊人。

lines.t: It’s hard to believe it’s the same place.
lines.cn: 很难相信这是同一个地方。

lines.t: And how do the neighbors feel now?
lines.cn: 邻居们现在感觉怎么样？

lines.t: Great pride, I would say.
lines.cn: 我会说，非常自豪。

lines.t: But what about the multitudes of visitors now crowding the streets?
lines.cn: 但现在街上挤满了大量游客，这又怎么说？

lines.t: Is everyone happy about that?
lines.cn: 大家对此都高兴吗？

lines.t: The tourists we receive are a blessing, as they have completely revitalized our local economy.
lines.cn: 我们接待的游客是一种福气，因为他们让本地经济彻底复苏了。

lines.t: Every visitor is warmly welcome.
lines.cn: 每一位访客我们都热情欢迎。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the passage say about a team of researchers at Northwestern University?

options.A: They have created the smallest remote-controlled walking robot in the world.
options.B: They are going to publish their research findings in the journal Science Robotics.
options.C: They are the first to build a robot that can bend, crawl, walk, turn and even jump.
options.D: They are engaged in research on a remote-controlled robot which uses special power.

questions.cn: 关于西北大学的一个研究团队，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们造出了世界上最小的遥控行走机器人。
optionsCn.B: 他们将在《科学·机器人学》期刊上发表研究成果。
optionsCn.C: 他们最先造出能弯曲、爬行、行走、转身甚至跳跃的机器人。
optionsCn.D: 他们在研究一种使用特殊动力的遥控机器人。

questions.stem: What did the researchers say about the robot they created?

options.A: It changes its shape by complex hardware.
options.B: It is operated by a special type of tiny motor.
options.C: It moves from one place to another by memory.
options.D: It is powered by the elastic property of its body.

questions.cn: 关于他们造出的机器人，研究者说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它靠复杂硬件改变形状。
optionsCn.B: 它由一个特殊类型的微型马达驱动。
optionsCn.C: 它靠记忆从一处移动到另一处。
optionsCn.D: 它由自身身体的弹性特性驱动。

questions.stem: What do the researchers expect their robots to do in the future?

options.A: Replace humans in exploratory tasks.
options.B: Perform tasks in tightly confined spaces.
options.C: Explore the structure of clogged arteries.
options.D: Assist surgeons in highly complex surgery.

questions.cn: 研究者期待他们的机器人在未来做什么？

optionsCn.A: 在探索性任务中取代人类。
optionsCn.B: 在狭小受限空间里执行任务。
optionsCn.C: 探查堵塞动脉的结构。
optionsCn.D: 在高度复杂的手术中协助外科医生。

lines.t: Researchers in the US have created a remote-controlled robot that is so small it can walk on the top of a US penny.
lines.cn: 美国研究者造出了一个遥控机器人，它小到能在一枚美国一美分硬币的顶面上行走。

lines.t: In research published in the journal Science Robotics, a team at Northwestern University said the crab-like robot is 0.5mm wide.
lines.cn: 在发表于《科学·机器人学》期刊的研究中，西北大学的一个团队说，这个螃蟹状的机器人宽 0.5 毫米。

lines.t: Researchers described it as the smallest-ever remote-controlled walking robot.
lines.cn: 研究者称它是有史以来最小的遥控行走机器人。

lines.t: The tiny robot can bend, twist, crawl, walk, turn, and even jump without the use of complex hardware or special power.
lines.cn: 这个微型机器人无需复杂的硬件或特殊动力，就能弯曲、扭转、爬行、行走、转身，甚至跳跃。

lines.t: The engineers said this is because the robot is powered by the elastic property of its body.
lines.cn: 工程师们说，这是因为该机器人由其身体的弹性特性驱动。

lines.t: To construct the robot, the researchers used a shape-memory alloy material that transforms to its remembered shape when heated.
lines.cn: 为制造这个机器人，研究者使用了一种形状记忆合金材料，受热时它会变回记忆中的形状。

lines.t: Using a laser, the team is able to heat the robot at specific parts of its body, causing it to change shape.
lines.cn: 团队用激光加热机器人身体的特定部位，使其改变形状。

lines.t: As the robot deforms and goes back to its original shape, it creates movement from one place to another.
lines.cn: 当机器人变形并恢复原状时，就产生了从一处到另一处的移动。

lines.t: “Because these structures are so tiny, the rate of cooling is very fast,” project lead Professor John A. Rogers said.
lines.cn: 项目负责人约翰·A. 罗杰斯教授说：“由于这些结构极其微小，冷却速度非常快。”

lines.t: “In fact, reducing the sizes of these robots allows them to run faster.”
lines.cn: “事实上，缩小这些机器人的尺寸反而能让它们跑得更快。”

lines.t: While the research is still in the exploratory phase, the team believes that technology could lead to micro-sized robots that can perform practical tasks in tightly confined spaces.
lines.cn: 尽管研究仍处于探索阶段，团队相信这项技术可能带来能在狭小受限空间内执行实际任务的微型机器人。

lines.t: “You might imagine microrobots as agents to repair or assemble small structures or machines in industry or as surgical assistants to clear clogged arteries, to stop internal bleeding, or to eliminate cancerous tumours-all in minimally invasive procedures,” Rogers said.
lines.cn: 罗杰斯说：“你可以把微型机器人想象成工业中修理或组装小型结构或机器的执行者，或者想象成外科助手，用于疏通堵塞的动脉、止住内出血，或消除癌性肿瘤——全部以微创方式完成。”

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say she did on her ride to the Isles of Scilly?

options.A: She threw up in the bathroom.
options.B: She slept during the entire ride.
options.C: She dozed off for a few minutes.
options.D: She boasted of her marathon race.

questions.cn: 讲话者说她在去锡利群岛的路上做了什么？

optionsCn.A: 她在洗手间里呕吐。
optionsCn.B: 她在整个航程中都在睡觉。
optionsCn.C: 她打了几分钟盹。
optionsCn.D: 她炫耀自己的马拉松比赛。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the passage about elite sleepers?

options.A: They are mostly immune to cognitive impairment.
options.B: They can sleep soundly during a rough ride at sea.
options.C: They are genetically determined to need less sleep.
options.D: They constitute about 13 percent of the population.

questions.cn: 关于精英级睡眠者，我们从文章中了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们大多不受认知损伤影响。
optionsCn.B: 他们能在海上颠簸航行时睡得很香。
optionsCn.C: 他们在基因上被设定为需要更少的睡眠。
optionsCn.D: 他们约占人口的 13%。

questions.stem: What has the speaker been trying to find out over the past year?

options.A: Whether there is a way to reach elite status.
options.B: Whether it is possible to modify one’s genes.
options.C: Whether having a baby impacts one’s passion.
options.D: Whether one can train themselves to sleep less.

questions.cn: 过去一年，讲话者一直在试图弄清什么？

optionsCn.A: 是否有办法达到精英级状态。
optionsCn.B: 是否有可能修改自己的基因。
optionsCn.C: 生孩子是否影响一个人的热情。
optionsCn.D: 人能否训练自己少睡。

questions.stem: What has the speaker discovered after a year of tough scientific study?

options.A: It is in fact quite possible to nurture a passion for sleep.
options.B: Babies can severely disrupt their parents’ sleep patterns.
options.C: Being forced to rise early differs from being an early bird.
options.D: New parents are forced to jump out of bed at the crack of dawn.

questions.cn: 经过一年艰苦的科学研究，讲话者发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 培养对睡眠的热情其实很可行。
optionsCn.B: 婴儿会严重打乱父母的睡眠模式。
optionsCn.C: 被迫早起与做早起型人是两回事。
optionsCn.D: 新手父母被迫天亮就跳下床。

lines.t: I don’t want to boast or anything, but I have always considered myself something of an elite sleeper.
lines.cn: 我不想自夸，但我一直自认为算是个精英级睡眠者。

lines.t: Given the opportunity, I will sleep for marathon stretches, and can doze through the most extreme situations.
lines.cn: 只要有机会，我就能一口气睡很久，还能在最极端的情况下打盹。

lines.t: On one very rough ferry crossing, on the route to the Isles of Scilly, for example, my traveling companion spent the entire 3-hour-ride throwing up in the bathroom, while I dozed happily on a plastic chair.
lines.cn: 比如有一次去锡利群岛的渡轮颠簸得非常厉害，我的旅伴整整三个小时的航程都在洗手间里呕吐，而我却在一张塑料椅上睡得香甜。

lines.t: Unfortunately, it has come to my attention that I am not an elite sleeper after all.
lines.cn: 遗憾的是，我注意到我其实并不是精英级睡眠者。

lines.t: It seems I am just lazy, because elite sleepers are defined as the approximately 3 percent of the population who are biologically programmed to need less sleep than the rest of us.
lines.cn: 看来我只是懒，因为精英级睡眠者指的是约占人口 3% 的那部分人，他们天生就被设定为比我们其他人需要更少的睡眠。

lines.t: According to a study that came out in March, elite sleepers have rare genetic changes, which means they can sleep fewer hours than mere mortals, without any risk of cognitive decline.
lines.cn: 根据三月发表的一项研究，精英级睡眠者带有罕见的基因变异，这意味着他们能比凡人睡更少的时间，而不承担任何认知衰退的风险。

lines.t: It may not be possible to change your own genes, but can you train yourself to need less sleep?
lines.cn: 改变自己的基因也许不可能，但你能训练自己少睡一点吗？

lines.t: Is there a nonbiological way to reach elite sleeper status?
lines.cn: 有没有非生物学的方式能达到精英级睡眠者的状态？

lines.t: I have spent the past year trying to answer that question.
lines.cn: 过去一年我一直在试着回答这个问题。

lines.t: Not for fun, I should add, but because having a baby has severely disrupted my sleep, for which I still have a great passion.
lines.cn: 我得补充一句，不是为了好玩，而是因为有了孩子严重打乱了我的睡眠，而我对睡眠依然满怀热爱。

lines.t: For a while, I assumed I’d be forced to become one of those people who jump out of bed at the crack of dawn.
lines.cn: 有一阵子，我以为自己将被迫成为那种天一亮就跳下床的人。

lines.t: After a year of tough scientific study, however, I have discovered being forced to get up early in the morning is very different from being an early bird.
lines.cn: 然而，经过一年艰苦的科学研究，我发现被迫早起和真正做个早起型的人是两回事。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggest?

options.A: We have poor awareness of how many controversial issues are being debated.
options.B: No one knows better than yourself what you are thinking about at the moment.
options.C: No one can change your opinions more than those who speak in a convincing tone.
options.D: We are likely to underestimate how much we can be swayed by a convincing article.

questions.cn: 《实验心理学季刊》上的新论文表明了什么？

optionsCn.A: 我们对正在被讨论的争议话题数量知之甚少。
optionsCn.B: 没有人比自己更清楚此刻自己心里在想什么。
optionsCn.C: 没有人比那些用有说服力语气说话的人更能改变你的观点。
optionsCn.D: 我们很可能低估一篇有说服力的文章对我们影响的程度。

questions.stem: What happened when the students read a text that argued against their own initial position?

options.A: Their belief about physical punishment changed.
options.B: Their memory pushed them toward a current belief.
options.C: The memory of their initial belief came back to them.
options.D: Their experiences of physical punishment haunted them.

questions.cn: 当学生读到反对自己初始立场的文章时，发生了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们对体罚的看法改变了。
optionsCn.B: 他们的记忆把他们推向当前看法。
optionsCn.C: 他们对初始看法的记忆回来了。
optionsCn.D: 他们遭受体罚的经历困扰着他们。

questions.stem: What did the researchers concede concerning their findings?

options.A: They apparently have little to do with moderate beliefs.
options.B: They don’t reflect the change of view on physical punishment.
options.C: They may not apply to changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs.
options.D: They are unlikely to alter people’s position without more evidence.

questions.cn: 关于他们的发现，研究者承认了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它们显然与温和的看法没什么关系。
optionsCn.B: 它们不反映关于体罚观点的变化。
optionsCn.C: 它们可能不适用于极端或根深蒂固信念的改变。
optionsCn.D: 没有更多证据，它们不太可能改变人们的立场。

lines.t: If you read an article about a controversial issue, do you think you’d realise if it had changed your beliefs?
lines.cn: 如果你读到一篇关于争议话题的文章，你觉得你会意识到它已经改变了你的看法吗？

lines.t: No one knows your own mind like you do-it seems obvious that you would know if your beliefs had shifted.
lines.cn: 没有人比你更了解自己的想法——你显然应该知道自己看法有没有转变。

lines.t: And yet a new paper in the Quarterly Journal of Experimental Psychology suggests that we actually have very poor awareness of our own belief change, meaning that we will tend to underestimate how much we’ve been swayed by a convincing article.
lines.cn: 然而《实验心理学季刊》上的一篇新论文表明，我们对自己看法发生改变的觉察其实很差，这意味着我们往往会低估自己被一篇有说服力的文章影响的程度。

lines.t: The researchers recruited over two hundred undergraduates across two studies and focused on their beliefs about whether physical punishment of kids is an effective form of discipline.
lines.cn: 研究者招募了两百多名本科生，做了两项研究，聚焦于他们对“体罚孩子是否是有效管教方式”的看法。

lines.t: The students reported their initial beliefs about whether physical punishment is an effective way to discipline a child on a scale from “1” completely disbelieve to “9” completely believe.
lines.cn: 学生们先报告了对“体罚是否是管教孩子的有效方式”的初始看法，按 1（完全不信）到 9（完全相信）评分。

lines.t: Several weeks later they were given one of two research-based texts to read: each was several pages long and either presented the arguments and data in favour of physical punishment or against it.
lines.cn: 几周后，他们被分配阅读两篇基于研究的文章之一：每篇都有好几页，一篇提出支持体罚的论据和数据，另一篇则反对。

lines.t: After this, the students answered some questions to test their comprehension and memory of the text.
lines.cn: 之后，学生回答一些问题，以检验他们对文章的理解和记忆。

lines.t: Then, the students again scored their belief in whether physical punishment is effective or not.
lines.cn: 接着，学生们再次为“体罚是否有效”的信念打分。

lines.t: Finally, the researchers asked them to recall what their belief had been at the start of the study.
lines.cn: 最后，研究者请他们回忆自己在研究开始时持有什么看法。

lines.t: The students’ belief about physical punishment changed when they read a text that argued against their own initial position.
lines.cn: 当学生读到反对自己初始立场的文章时，他们对体罚的看法确实发生了变化。

lines.t: Crucially, the memory of their initial belief was shifted in the direction of their new belief-in fact, their memory was closer to their current belief than their original belief.
lines.cn: 关键在于，他们对初始看法的记忆朝着新看法的方向发生了偏移——事实上，他们的记忆更接近当前看法，而不是最初看法。

lines.t: The more their belief had changed, the larger this memory bias tended to be, suggesting the students were relying on their current belief to deduce their initial belief.
lines.cn: 看法改变得越多，这种记忆偏差往往越大，这表明学生们是依据当前看法来推断自己最初的看法。

lines.t: The memory bias was unrelated to the measures of how well they’d understood or recalled the text, suggesting these factors didn’t play a role in memory of initial belief or awareness of belief change.
lines.cn: 这种记忆偏差与衡量他们理解和回忆文章程度的指标无关，说明这些因素并未影响对初始看法的记忆或对看法改变的觉察。

lines.t: The researchers concede that this research was about changes to mostly moderate beliefs-it’s likely the findings would be different in the context of changes to extreme or deeply held beliefs.
lines.cn: 研究者承认，这项研究针对的多是温和看法的改变——若涉及极端或根深蒂固的信念发生改变，结果很可能会不同。

lines.t: However, our beliefs on most topics are in the moderate range, and as we go about our daily lives reading informative material, these intriguing findings suggest we are mostly ignorant of how what we just read has updated and altered our own position.
lines.cn: 然而，我们在大多数话题上的看法都处于温和区间；而当我们在日常生活中阅读信息性材料时，这些有趣的发现表明：我们大多并不知道刚刚读到的东西如何更新并改变了我们自己的立场。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker conclude from her analysis of the Census Bureau’s data?

options.A: American moms have been increasingly inclined to live alone.
options.B: The American population has been on the rise in the past 25 years.
options.C: American motherhood has actually been on the decline.
options.D: The fertility rates in America have in fact been falling sharply.

questions.cn: 讲话者从她对人口普查局数据的分析中得出什么结论？

optionsCn.A: 美国妈妈越来越倾向于独居。
optionsCn.B: 过去 25 年美国人口一直在增长。
optionsCn.C: 美国的“为人母”比例实际上一直在下降。
optionsCn.D: 美国的生育率实际上一直在急剧下降。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is a positive consequence of the age shift in childbearing?

options.A: More new mothers tend to take greater care of their children.
options.B: More new mothers are economically able to raise children.
options.C: A larger proportion of women take pride in their children.
options.D: A larger proportion of women really enjoy motherhood.

questions.cn: 讲话者说生育年龄后移的积极后果是什么？

optionsCn.A: 更多新妈妈往往更用心照顾孩子。
optionsCn.B: 更多新妈妈在经济上有能力抚养孩子。
optionsCn.C: 更大比例的女性为子女感到自豪。
optionsCn.D: 更大比例的女性真正享受为人母。

questions.stem: What might be one explanation for the rise in retail spending on Mother’s Day?

options.A: The meaning of motherhood has changed considerably.
options.B: More and more mothers go shopping to treat themselves.
options.C: More mothers have adult children celebrating the holiday.
options.D: The number of American mothers has been growing steadily.

questions.cn: 母亲节零售支出上升的一个可能解释是什么？

optionsCn.A: 为人母的含义已发生很大变化。
optionsCn.B: 越来越多的妈妈通过购物犒赏自己。
optionsCn.C: 更多妈妈有已成年的子女为自己庆祝节日。
optionsCn.D: 美国妈妈的数量一直在稳步增长。

lines.t: As the American population grows, so does the number of American moms.
lines.cn: 随着美国人口增长，美国妈妈的数量也在增加。

lines.t: But, more than a century after Mother’s Day became an official holiday, even as that number increases, the share of the American population who are mothers is at the lowest point in a quarter century.
lines.cn: 但是，在母亲节成为正式节日一个多世纪之后，尽管妈妈的人数在增加，母亲在美国人口中所占的比例却处于四分之一个世纪以来的最低点。

lines.t: It’s frequently noted that fertility rates are falling sharply in richer countries.
lines.cn: 人们常提到，富裕国家的生育率正在急剧下降。

lines.t: But the less observed consequence of this trend is that a decline in births can also mean a decline in motherhood in general.
lines.cn: 但这一趋势较少被注意到的后果是：出生人数下降也可能意味着总体上“为人母”的比例下降。

lines.t: According to my analysis of data from the Census Bureau, the decline of American motherhood is real, occurring very quickly, and may continue for some time yet.
lines.cn: 根据我对人口普查局数据的分析，美国“为人母”比例的下降是真实的，发生得很快，而且可能还会持续一段时间。

lines.t: Not only are moms making up less of the population, but their characteristics are changing too, and in a way that might be linked to their proportional decline.
lines.cn: 不仅妈妈在人口中的占比变小，她们的特征也在变化，而这种变化可能与她们占比下降有关。

lines.t: Moms today tend to be older than in the past.
lines.cn: 如今的妈妈比过去更年长。

lines.t: Just looking at recent years, the change in age-specific birth rates has been drastic.
lines.cn: 仅看近几年，分年龄生育率的变化就相当剧烈。

lines.t: In just the past few years, the peak childbearing age range for American women has advanced from that of 25-29 to that of 30-34.
lines.cn: 就在过去几年里，美国女性的生育高峰年龄段已从 25 至 29 岁后移到 30 至 34 岁。

lines.t: Meanwhile, childbearing among women under 20 has fallen by half or more, while childbearing among women 35 and older is rising.
lines.cn: 与此同时，20 岁以下女性的生育下降了至少一半，而 35 岁及以上女性的生育则在上升。

lines.t: One positive consequence of this age shift is that a larger proportion of new mothers are economically prepared to raise children.
lines.cn: 这种年龄后移的一个积极后果是：更大比例的新妈妈在经济上已具备抚养孩子的条件。

lines.t: Less positively, however, many women find that, as they age, they can’t have as many kids as they would like.
lines.cn: 但不太乐观的是，许多女性发现随着年龄增长，她们无法生育自己想要的孩子数量。

lines.t: Plus, having children later in life can increase the risk of health complications.
lines.cn: 此外，较晚生育会增加出现健康并发症的风险。

lines.t: These finer points aside, one major consequence of the older moms trend is that fewer years of a woman’s life are spent as a mother.
lines.cn: 撇开这些细节不谈，“妈妈更年长”这一趋势的一个主要后果是：女性一生中作为母亲度过的年头变少了。

lines.t: This means that, at any given time, a larger share of women, and thus of the whole population, will report not having children in government surveys.
lines.cn: 这意味着，在任何时点，都会有更大比例的女性——从而也是更大比例的总人口——在政府调查中报告自己没有孩子。

lines.t: In other words, later motherhood means less motherhood.
lines.cn: 换句话说，更晚做母亲意味着“为人母”的阶段更短。

lines.t: Even as motherhood rates decline, Mother’s Day, of course, will endure.
lines.cn: 尽管为人母的比例在下降，母亲节当然还会延续。

lines.t: In fact, despite the demographic shift, retail spending on the holiday appears to be rising.
lines.cn: 事实上，尽管人口结构发生变化，这个节日的零售支出似乎在上升。

lines.t: It is hard to say if Mother’s Day spending is rising more than one would expect, given that the American population keeps growing, but one factor might be that the proportion of women who are the mothers of adult children is rising.
lines.cn: 考虑到美国人口持续增长，很难说母亲节的支出是否比预期增长得更多，但一个因素可能是：其子女已成年母亲的比例在上升。

lines.t: And those adult children may spend more generously when it comes to celebrating the moms they no longer live with.
lines.cn: 而那些已成年的子女，在庆祝不再与他们同住的妈妈时，或许会花得更慷慨。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does NASA’s 1989 paper claim houseplants can do?

options.A: Add to indoor toxic pollutants.
options.B: Absorb poisonous chemicals.
options.C: Beautify the home environment.
options.D: Soak up surrounding moisture.

questions.cn: NASA 1989 年的论文声称室内植物能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 增加室内的有毒污染物。
optionsCn.B: 吸收有毒化学物质。
optionsCn.C: 美化家居环境。
optionsCn.D: 吸收周围的水分。

questions.stem: What is said to be the problem with NASA’s study reported in its 1989 paper?

options.A: NASA did experiments in sealed containers resembling the super insulated offices of 1970s.
options.B: It was based on experiments under conditions unlike those in most homes or offices.
options.C: NASA conducted tests in outer space whose environment is different from ours.
options.D: It drew its conclusion without any contrastive data from other experiments.

questions.cn: 据说 NASA 1989 年论文所报告研究的问题是什么？

optionsCn.A: NASA 在与 20 世纪 70 年代超绝热办公室相似的密闭容器中做实验。
optionsCn.B: 它基于的条件与大多数家庭或办公室不同。
optionsCn.C: NASA 在外太空做测试，那里环境与我们不同。
optionsCn.D: 它得出结论时没有任何其他实验的对照数据。

questions.stem: What is the finding of a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years?

options.A: Natural ventilation proves much more efficient for cleaning the air than houseplants.
options.B: Houseplants disperse chemical compounds more quickly with people moving around.
options.C: Natural ventilation turns out to be most effective with doors and windows wide open.
options.D: Houseplants in a normal environment rarely have any adverse impact on the air.

questions.cn: 一项对 30 年间数十项研究的新评估发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 自然通风在净化空气方面比室内植物高效得多。
optionsCn.B: 人多走动时，室内植物能更快地扩散化合物。
optionsCn.C: 门窗大开时，自然通风效果最佳。
optionsCn.D: 普通环境中的室内植物很少对空气产生不良影响。

questions.stem: What does NASA’s sealed experiment recommendation exemplify in scientists’ pursuit of truth?

options.A: The root cause for misinterpretations of scientific findings.
options.B: The difficulty in understanding what’s actually happening.
options.C: The steps to be taken in arriving at any conclusion with certainty.
options.D: The necessity of continually reexamining and challenging findings.

questions.cn: 在科学家追求真相的过程中，NASA 密闭实验的建议例证了什么？

optionsCn.A: 对科学发现产生误解的根本原因。
optionsCn.B: 理解实际发生了什么有多么困难。
optionsCn.C: 为确凿得出结论而应采取的步骤。
optionsCn.D: 不断重新检视和质疑结论的必要性。

lines.t: Since NASA published a paper in 1989 claiming that houseplants can soak up pollution and toxic chemicals, businesses and homeowners have increasingly invested in greenery to help clean their air.
lines.cn: 自从美国航空航天局（NASA）1989 年发表论文声称室内植物能吸收污染和有毒化学物质以来，企业和房主越来越多地投资绿植来净化空气。

lines.t: But, a new analysis suggests it could actually take more than 1,000 plants per square meter to gain a benefit any greater than simply opening a couple of windows.
lines.cn: 但一项新分析表明，要想获得比“开几扇窗”更好的效果，实际上每平方米可能需要 1000 株以上的植物。

lines.t: The problem lies in the fact that NASA conducted their tests in sealed containers that do not simulate the conditions in most people’s homes or offices.
lines.cn: 问题在于，NASA 的测试是在密闭容器中进行的，并未模拟大多数人家中或办公室里的条件。

lines.t: The space agency was primarily concerned about keeping the air fresh for astronauts cut off in biospheres or space stations and helping to combat “sick building syndrome”, which had become a problem due to the super insulated and energy efficient offices of the late 1970s.
lines.cn: 这家航天机构主要关心的是：为困在生物圈或空间站中的宇航员保持空气清新，以及帮助应对“病态建筑综合征”——由于 20 世纪 70 年代末超绝热、节能的办公楼，这个问题变得突出。

lines.t: By the early 1980s, workers regularly complained of skin rashes, sleepiness, headaches, and allergies as they breathed in toxic chemicals from paints and plastics.
lines.cn: 到 80 年代初，工人们常抱怨因吸入来自油漆和塑料的有毒化学物质而出现皮疹、困倦、头痛和过敏。

lines.t: NASA found that certain plants could remove chemicals from the air, and even today, garden centers recommend the plants for air cleaning properties.
lines.cn: NASA 发现某些植物能清除空气中的化学物质；甚至在今天，园艺店仍以净化空气的特性来推荐这些植物。

lines.t: However, a new evaluation of dozens of studies spanning 30 years found that houseplants in a normal environment have little impact.
lines.cn: 然而，一项对 30 年间数十项研究的新评估发现，普通环境中的室内植物作用微乎其微。

lines.t: In fact, natural ventilation is far better at cleaning the air.
lines.cn: 事实上，自然通风在净化空气方面要好得多。

lines.t: The researchers also calculated the clean air delivery rate for plants in the studies they analyzed and found that the rate at which plants disperse the compounds was well below the usual rate of air exchange in a normal building, caused by the movement of people coming and going, opening doors and windows.
lines.cn: 研究者还计算了其所分析研究中植物的“洁净空气输送率”，发现植物扩散化合物的速率远低于普通建筑中通常的换气速率——后者由人来人往、开关门窗所产生。

lines.t: Many of the studies did show a reduction in the concentration of volatile organic compounds over time, which is likely why people have seized on them to praise the air purifying virtues of plants.
lines.cn: 许多研究确实显示挥发性有机化合物的浓度随时间下降，这大概就是人们抓住它们、盛赞植物净化空气功效的原因。

lines.t: But the researchers’ calculation showed it would take 10 to 1,000 plants per square meter of floor space to compete with the air cleaning capacity of a building’s air handling system or even just a couple of open windows in a house.
lines.cn: 但研究者的计算显示，要与一栋建筑的空气处理系统、甚至只与家里开几扇窗的净化能力相当，每平方米地面需要 10 到 1000 株植物。

lines.t: In contrast, NASA’s sealed experiment recommended one pot plant per 100 square feet.
lines.cn: 相比之下，NASA 的密闭实验建议每 100 平方英尺放一盆植物。

lines.t: This is certainly an example of how scientific findings can be misleading or misinterpreted over time.
lines.cn: 这无疑是科学发现会随时间被误导或误读的一个例子。

lines.t: But it’s also a great example of how scientific research should continually reexamine and question findings to get closer to the ground truth of understanding what’s actually happening.
lines.cn: 但它也是一个绝好的例子，说明科学研究应当不断重新检视和质疑已有结论，以更接近“实际发生了什么”的真相。
